sources.title: GPT-5.6: Frontier intelligence that scales with your ambition
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. July 9 general-availability announcement identifies Sol as the flagship GPT-5.6 tier with API, ChatGPT and Codex access, reasoning and programmatic tool calling. It describes Sol, Terra and Luna as different model sizes but supplies no nominal total/active counts or named base with disclosed counts.

sources.title: GPT-5.6 Sol — API model documentation
sources.evidence: Fresh original Markdown fetched HTTP 200 October 27 at 16:22 UTC and independently reopened through official documentation. Exact gpt-5.6-sol snapshot, gpt-5.6 routing alias, 1,050,000 context, 922,000 maximum input and 128,000 output tokens; text/image input, text output, reasoning and function calling. No total/active parameter field; API request parameters are not weight counts.

sources.title: GPT-5.6 System Card
sources.evidence: Fresh original PDF fetched HTTP 200 October 27 at 15:42 UTC; reopened training section and exact Sol evaluation tables, and searched full extracted text. No nominal total/active count or architectural classification is stated. Parameter-term hits concern tuning hyperparameters for a separate small-model training benchmark; a billion-dollar risk scenario is unrelated to model size.

sources.title: How GPT-5.6 fuses frontier intelligence with frontier efficiency
sources.evidence: Reopened original July 29 engineering article October 27. It describes load balancing, forward passes, KV caching and speculative decoding without a total/active count or explicit Transformer/dense/MoE designation. Its one billion active users refers to users. Architecture/size experiments concern a separate draft model, and accelerator capacity and serving improvements do not establish Sol size.

sources.title: GPT-6 Astra System Card
sources.evidence: Fresh original PDF fetched HTTP 200 October 27 at 15:42 UTC; reopened September 3 training section, exact GPT-5.6 Sol comparison tables and full-text count search. Tables report safety/capability scores, not total or active parameters. NanoGPT hyperparameter tuning is a separate small-scale training task, not a Sol size disclosure.

sources.title: Addendum to GPT-6 Astra System Card: GPT-6.1 Sol
sources.evidence: Fresh original PDF fetched HTTP 200 October 27 at 15:42 UTC; reopened September 29 addendum, training section and exact GPT-5.6 Sol comparison columns. The reviewed safety, biological and cybersecurity tables contain scores and no total/active parameter counts; full-text parameter-term search found none.

sources.title: File inputs — OpenAI API
sources.evidence: Responses accepts input_file; vision-capable models receive extracted PDF text and page images. Chat Completions accepts PDF file parts. Together with the exact Sol endpoint/vision listing, this supports PDF as an API input format.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Sections 2.2, 3.3 and 9.1 grant limited access to the hosted service, restrict reverse engineering and reserve OpenAI’s rights. Supports a descriptive Proprietary classification for the documented hosted model, not an open-weight license.

sources.title: Previewing GPT-5.6 Sol: a next-generation model
sources.evidence: June 26 announcement describes a limited API/Codex preview restricted to a small group of trusted partners, with broader availability still planned. Distinguishes the preview from the July 9 public launch. The indexed primary page was readable; direct HTTP retrieval returned 403.

sources.title: OpenAI API changelog
sources.evidence: July 9 explicitly releases gpt-5.6-sol and the gpt-5.6 alias. August 6 updates chat-latest while recommending production Sol separately; August 13 calls Ultrafast a service tier, not a new checkpoint.

sources.title: ChatGPT release notes
sources.evidence: August 6 describes an updated Sol in the ChatGPT chat experience and explicitly excludes Work/Codex from that change. This does not establish a replacement of the gpt-5.6-sol production API snapshot.

sources.title: Prompt caching — OpenAI API
sources.evidence: Current guide covers GPT-5.6 and later and explains reuse of intermediate KV states, but does not specify this model’s network architecture or counts.

sources.title: Prompt Caching 201
sources.evidence: Archived February 18 article explains Transformer attention but explicitly limits its applicability to models before GPT-5.6. It cannot establish GPT-5.6 Sol’s architecture.

sources.title: GPT-5.6 Preview System Card
sources.evidence: Reopened original June 26 preview card October 27. Model Data and Training describes data sources and reasoning reinforcement learning, without a nominal total or active count or a counted named base. A billion-dollar cyber-risk scenario is unrelated to parameters.

sources.title: Kimi K3: Open Frontier Intelligence — original Moonshot technical report
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. Table 1 has explicit Total Parameters and Activated Parameters rows, but only for Kimi K2 and Kimi K3. Tables 2, 3 and 5 identify GPT-5.6 Sol exactly and report evaluation scores, with no Sol parameter row. Kimi counts and cost comparisons cannot be transferred to Sol.

sources.title: Estimating the Parameter Counts of the Claude 5 and GPT-5.6 Families
sources.evidence: New numerical lead reopened October 27. July 31 original probe analysis lists Sol at 1.93T IKP-effective parameters with a 559B–6.7T interval. Section 2 explicitly defines this as calibrated knowledge capacity rather than a true weight count; it supplies neither a published nominal total specification nor an active count. Its inferred lineage is behavioral, not a developer statement.

developer.note: OpenAI publishes the model and its system card.

family.note: The generation is GPT-5.6; Sol is its capability tier. Corrects baseline gpt-sol.

release_date.note: Public/general API release. June 26 was a restricted trusted-partner preview, not the broad release; later ChatGPT and serving-tier changes do not change this date.

open_weights.note: The documented release is a hosted service under OpenAI terms; the reviewed release and model documentation provide no downloadable Sol weights.

license.note: Descriptive classification of the hosted model under OpenAI service terms; no open-weight license is documented.

parameters_b.note: October 27 parameter re-audit reopened the launch, exact API reference, preview/final cards, later OpenAI comparisons and engineering article, then searched for newer total counts and named-base lineage. No supported nominal total or counted base was found. Moonshot Kimi K3 comparison columns give Sol scores, not size; Eigenigma 1.93T is explicitly an IKP-effective knowledge estimate, not a weight count. Draft-model experiments and hardware capacity do not supply Sol counts.

active_parameters_b.note: Rechecked separately October 27. No explicit nominal active count was found in exact Sol documentation or original OpenAI/Moonshot comparison tables. Moonshot active rows apply only to its own Kimi models; the engineering article counts active users, and Eigenigma estimates knowledge capacity. No active value is inferred from a total, architecture label or serving performance.

architecture.note: No sufficient exact-model structural evidence found. KV caching and next-token forward passes alone do not establish Transformer; sub-networks do not establish MoE. The named architecture experiments are for a separate draft model. The older Transformer caching article explicitly excludes GPT-5.6+.

context_window.note: Exact API documentation states total context 1,050,000, maximum input 922,000 and maximum output 128,000 tokens. Product chat limits are separate.

modalities.note: Text/image are native API inputs; PDF is a supported file format converted to text/page images. Image-generation tool access is not native image output. Audio/video endpoints are not supported.

reasoning.note: API supports reasoning tokens and effort none, low, medium, high, xhigh and max. An optional none setting does not negate reasoning support.

tool_call.note: Exact model lists function calling and Responses tools; launch changelog also documents programmatic tool calling.

description.value: GPT-5.6 model for reasoning, coding, research, and tool-based work.
description.note: Replaces promotional wording with supported uses without asserting benchmark superiority or undisclosed structure.

patch.notes: July 9, 2026 is the public API release; June 26 was a restricted partner preview. The gpt-5.6 alias routes to gpt-5.6-sol; documentation lists no dated Sol snapshot. Context is 1,050,000 tokens, with explicit limits of 922,000 input and 128,000 output. PDF input is API text/page-image extraction. The August 6 ChatGPT update and August 13 Ultrafast service-tier announcement do not identify a new production Sol API checkpoint. Total and active parameters remain undisclosed; knowledge-capacity estimates and separate draft-model experiments are not Sol parameter counts. Exact architecture remains unverified.

summary: October 27 parameter-only re-audit preserves null/undisclosed total and active counts after reopening current primary sources, independently reviewing later OpenAI and Moonshot exact-model comparison tables, and targeted searches for new counts and explicit counted-base lineage. Rejects the newly located 1.93T IKP-effective estimate because its author explicitly distinguishes knowledge capacity from actual weights. Adds explicit null parameter patches and provenance; preserves the other 12 assessments and original non-parameter corrections.
